methods.label: Thicken the segment
methods.sourceMethod: LIVE worked explanation and AoPS geometric solution: a radius-one neighborhood of a length-five segment, decomposed into a rectangle and two semicircles.

annotationRationale: The question tests translating complex addition into a geometric region and decomposing that region to compute its area. The length five belongs to the segment, rather than to every possible z1.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the essential task is identifying and measuring a planar region.

review.questionCheck: The region is exactly the radius-one neighborhood of a segment of length 5. Its area is 10+π≈13.14, whose nearest integer is 13, choice A. The statement, choices and key agree; no question figure or grading conflict is supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. The LIVE and AoPS geometric explanations use the same rectangle-and-semicircles route, retained as segment-neighborhood-area. A second method would add little to this short calculation.
review.annotationCheck: Complex addition interpreted geometrically and composite-area decomposition are appropriate assessed concepts. Point representation, distance and the elementary area formulas are appropriately supporting.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the essential task is identifying and measuring a planar region.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The equivalence |z−z₁|≤1 correctly identifies the union of disks. Orthogonal projection partitions it into a 5×2 rectangle and two outward radius-one semicircles, with only boundary overlaps. The area and rounding are correct.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits both third-party explanations using source-informed-original. The candidate independently justifies the shape and avoids the AoPS reference's erroneous statement that every z₁ has magnitude 5; 5 is the segment's length.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The disk interpretation and nearest-point classification explain both the straight sides and endpoint caps. The decomposition is sufficiently explicit without a new diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All six immediate nodes are relevant: complex-plane representation, geometric addition/subtraction, coordinate distance, composite areas, rectangle area and circle area. The neighborhood description is fully derived, so it needs no additional specialized node.

N-CN.A.3 contributes no conjugate or quotient reasoning here. Rectangle-area links support multiplication and additivity; 7.G.B.4 supports circle-area use. Rectilinear/polygon standards do not fully cover the curved caps. Supplied rationales mentioning polar forms, conjugates, circumference derivations or solids do not establish such coverage.
